report: Source reassessment: the complete claim requires independent emitter selection of stable definition identities and semantic ordering before emission, including forward references, and forbids comparator sorting, renumbering or other repair. Both ordinary implementation associations are accounted for: sage_emit::emit_module constructs a fresh emitter, pre_register_mod traverses modules and their local definitions before emit_mod; sage_oracle::emit_crate likewise pre_register_module precedes emit_module. Both registration routines assign sequential IDs with duplicate checks, and local_id/normalize_def reuse the maps rather than allocate IDs during reference emission. Module, variant, field and argument iteration retain native semantic sequence; neither emitter consumes the other output. This supports the emitter-owned mechanism, not a universal determinism proof. The complete associated test set is the single explicit TODO service_spec function; it contains no behavioral assertion and is not counted as a determinism test. Its prerequisite is associating and reviewing complete independent repeated-fixture, forward-reference, deliberately reordered-item and namespace-kind evidence on both emitters. Those checks must detect identity/order changes; comparator non-repair and universal ordering stability remain unverified portions of this complete-evidence deferral, as in the historical rationale. Accepting this explicit TODO does not assert those scenarios or comparator guarantees are tested or complete. Baseline: I independently compared both full implementation files and the service_spec source against the supplied historical snapshots: all are exact byte matches, and the complete claim matches. I reassessed the current metadata, complete associated test body and emitter source, rather than treating the old verdict as execution evidence. Execution: I ran review start and the exact comparisons/source reads, and record for this report; no behavior tests or broad suites were run by me.
